div.head: Hl 12
div.ab: Gif man oþrum steop asette ðær mæn drincen, buton scylde, an eald riht scll' agelde þam þe þæt flet age, ⁊ VI scll' þam þe man þone steap aset, ⁊ cynge XII scll'.
Gif man oþrum steop asette ðær mæn drincen, buton scylde, an eald riht scll' agelde þam þe þæt flet age, ⁊ VI scll' þam þe man þone steap aset, ⁊ cynge XII scll'.
Gif man oþrum steop asette ðær mæn drincen buton scylde, an eald riht scƚƚ agelde þam þe þæt flet age, ⁊ VI scƚƚ þam þe man þone steap aset, ⁊ cynge XII scƚƚ.

Wenn jemand einem andren den Becher fortsetzt, wo Leute trinken, ohne [dessen] Verschulden, so gelte er nach altem Recht [1] Schll. demjenigen, der das Haus besitzt und 6 Schll. dem, welchem er den Becher wegsetzte und dem Könige 12 Schll.

If someone takes away another’s cup where people are drinking, without [the latter’s] fault, then let him pay according to old law [1] shilling to the one who owns the house and 6 shillings to the one whose cup he took away, and 12 shillings to the king.

If, where men are drinking, one man takes away the stoup of another, who has committed no offence, he shall pay, in accordance with established custom, a shilling to him who owns the house, 6 shillings to him whose stoup has been taken away, and 12 shillings to the king.

If anyone removes a cup from another where men are drinking, without provocation, he shall according to ancient law pay a shilling to him who owns the house, and six shillings to him whose cup was removed, and 12 shillings to the king.

If a person takes a cup from another where men are drinking without [the man from whom the cup was taken being at] fault, according to established right let him give a shilling to him who owns that house, and 6 shillings to him from whom the cup was taken, and 12 shillings to the king.

note.seg: Die Bussen für den Schutzherrn, für den direkt Beleidigten und das Strafgeldfixum wie in Hl 11. 13
The compensations for the protector and for the person directly insulted, and the fixed fine, as in Hl 11. 13
Vgl. Gl Biergelage 7b. Fortweisung des Trinkers zu niederem Platze oder aus dem Saale kennt Gilden- und Dänisches Witherlagsrecht; Pappenheim in Krit. Vierteljschr. 32 (1890) 79
Cf. Gl Biergelage 7b. The sending away of a drinker to a lower place or out of the hall is known to guild law and to the Danish law of the Witherlag; Pappenheim in Krit. Vierteljschr. 32 (1890) 79

Das von Price angeführte Bewerfen mit Bechern oder Beschütten mit Bier bei den Friesen (Wilda 779) steht ferner. Daraus abgeleitet: asettan of ‘entsetzen (eines Amtes)’. Toller s. v. steap bezweifelt also diese sonst unbelegte Übersetzung grundlos

The throwing of cups or drenching with beer among the Frisians, cited by Price (Wilda 779), is more remote. Derived from this: asettan of ‘to remove (from an office)’. Toller s. v. steap therefore doubts this otherwise unattested translation without reason

Nicht das Trinken der anderen Genossen soll als ‘schuldlos’ qualifiziert werden, wie Frühere übersetzen, sondern erheblich war nur, dass der éine Beleidigte keine Schuld hatte, die zur Missetat Anlass bot; ebenso Abt 86¹ und u. 13

It is not the drinking of the other companions that is to be qualified as ‘blameless’, as earlier scholars translate; what alone mattered was that the one person insulted bore no blame that gave occasion for the misdeed; likewise Abt 86¹ and below 13

‘Altes (s. d. Gl) Recht’, nicht in Ggs. zu ‘neuem’, sondern ‘erprobt, echt’; vgl. Wb ealdlandræden und in Wbb. die Composita ealdfeond (-geniðla, -gewinna) ‘Erzfeind’, ealdgecynd ‘Urnatur’, ealdhlaford ‘rechtmässiger Herr’, ealdmynster ‘Hauptkirche’, ealdwita ‘Hochweiser, höchst Vornehmer’; Toller weist Komposita ealdriht, ealdgeriht nach; so kann man auch hier éin Wort lesen

‘Old (see that word in Gl) law’, not in contrast to ‘new’, but ‘tried, genuine’; cf. Wb ealdlandræden and in the dictionaries the compounds ealdfeond (-geniðla, -gewinna) ‘arch-enemy’, ealdgecynd ‘original nature’, ealdhlaford ‘rightful lord’, ealdmynster ‘principal church’, ealdwita ‘most wise man, man of the highest rank’; Toller records the compounds ealdriht, ealdgeriht; so here too one may read a single word
For eald riht cf. Wiht. cap. 5, note 4.
